blurb:
Josie has the most ridiculously adorable floppy ears and a nubby little tail, and she would very much like you to come meet her. She's a six-year-old hound mix, about 35 pounds, and she runs on a 5-to-7 energy scale with the occasional zoomie burst thrown in for free.

She went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups immersive training program and came out knowing sit, stay, and more. She's been adopted once already, but the energy level wasn't a match for that family, so she's back and looking for someone who actually wants an active dog. She loves walks, loves people, and loves couch time after the walks. That's a solid deal.

She does best as an only dog and no cats. She hasn't met a lot of kids yet, but her foster thinks kids ten and up would be a good fit since she plays hard and can get a little mouthy during play. Nothing mean, just enthusiastic. She's currently in a foster home and doing well there while she waits.

If you've got the energy to keep up with her and want a genuinely sweet, funny dog who will be all in on whatever you're doing, Josie is worth a visit. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Submit an application on their website or stop by to meet her.
scoring_notes:
• Returned-once narrative paired with Prison Pups training creates a sympathetic, redemption-ready profile
• Active, playful personality with clear energy-match framing helps readers self-select, improving fit quality
• Prior adoption return and only-dog/no-cat restrictions suggest she has been waiting longer than her age implies

blurb:
Bolton came into Mostly Mutts underweight, with thin fur, and no easy past to speak of. That was then. Now he's 64 pounds of goofy, sniff-everything, light-up-the-room energy living in a foster home and doing great. He's nine years old, which means he's got all the personality of a dog who's been through some things and come out the other side genuinely happy.

His foster says he makes every room better just by walking into it. He's a hound mix, so his nose is basically always running the show. Give him a yard to explore and he's going to be very busy and very pleased about it. He can go from zooming around playing tag with another dog to flopping down next to you on the couch in about three minutes flat. That range is a feature, not a bug.

He's good with dogs and has shown it in his foster home, so if you have a laid-back pup at home, it's worth a meet and greet. No cats, and best to skip homes with toddlers since he's a big guy and could bump a small kid over without meaning to. Kids around 8 to 12 have been a great fit so far. He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so he's got manners to go with the silliness.

Mostly Mutts handles adoptions by application. Head to their website to get started, or visit them in Kennesaw to meet Bolton in person.
scoring_notes:
• Senior dog comeback story — arrived underweight and neglected, now thriving — delivers the emotional arc readers remember
• Prison Pups training credential adds credibility and differentiates him from typical shelter dogs
• Age, size, and cat/toddler restrictions narrow the pool significantly, implying a longer road to placement

blurb:
Meeko is 12 years old, 33 pounds, and his foster straight up calls him a treasure. That's a real quote. The woman fostering him says he sometimes seems to read her mind. He also has a favorite security blanket, which is an old towel, and honestly that detail alone should tell you everything you need to know about this dog.

He's a Jack Russell and Greyhound mix, which is a combination that should not work as well as it apparently does. He knows sit, down, stay, come, go, wait, and something called last call for a pre-bedtime potty break. He walks nicely on a leash, doesn't jump on strangers, and has good crate manners. He's current on vaccinations, neutered, microchipped, and already had a dental cleaning. He came in from animal control and landed in foster care, where he has been, by all accounts, a very good boy.

He'd do best as an only dog and in a calm, quieter home. Mostly Mutts recommends kids 15 and up. He might bark at something unfamiliar at first, but he settles right in once he gets comfortable.

If you want a mellow, smart, deeply lovable senior dog who will park himself next to you with his old towel and just be happy to be there, Meeko is your guy. Visit Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw or apply on their website.
scoring_notes:
• Security-blanket detail and foster's 'treasure' quote are ready-made headline moments that drive emotional reader engagement
• At 12 years old with only-dog and teen-household requirements, he faces the steepest adoption odds of the group — urgency is real
• Animal control intake to foster care at senior age signals an extended shelter journey and makes his story the most time-sensitive feature candidate

blurb:
Dionne is three months old, four and a half pounds, and named after a Clueless character, which already tells you the volunteers at Mostly Mutts have good taste. She and her sister were pulled from animal control, spent time in a foster home getting socialized, and have now landed back at the shelter where the volunteers have been happily spoiling them. She's ready to find a home of her own.

She gets along great with her sister, which is a good sign for anyone who already has a cat at home. She's litter trained, curious, playful when she's got energy, and genuinely happy to curl up on a person when she needs to recharge. That's a pretty solid kitten personality. No major quirks, no complicated history. She's just a young, friendly cat who wants a good spot to land.

The one thing to know upfront: Mostly Mutts requires her spay to be completed as she grows, and they'll cover that cost through their approved vet network. That makes this a local adoption only, North Metro Atlanta area. Her adoption fee is $175. If you're ready for a kitten and want one with a solid temperament and a good start, Dionne is worth a visit to Mostly Mutts.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (North Metro Atlanta area — local adoptions only)
scoring_notes:
• Clueless-themed name and easygoing temperament give this kitten instant personality and reader appeal
• Clean, uncomplicated profile with multi-cat compatibility makes her a low-risk, high-reward adoption
• Recently transitioned from foster back to shelter, indicating a short overall wait with moderate urgency

blurb:
Two pounds of cat with a Seinfeld-themed name and apparently zero dislikes. Jerry is about two and a half months old, came into Mostly Mutts through animal control with his siblings, and has been living his best foster life ever since. He's small enough to fit in your jacket pocket, but he's already figured out the full routine: chase something, wrestle a sibling, nap hard, repeat.

What's notable about Jerry is how well-rounded he already is for a kitten his age. He's been around dogs in his foster home and handled it fine. There are kids in the house too, the youngest around eleven, and he gets along with them without issue. He's litter trained. He goes from full chaos mode to curled-up-on-your-lap mode without much in between. That's a pretty easy cat to live with.

He does need you to finish his kitten vaccination series as he grows, and his spay or neuter will be required as well. Because Mostly Mutts covers that cost through their approved vets, this is a local adoption only. If you're in the North Metro Atlanta area and thinking about adding a kitten to the mix, Jerry's worth going to meet. His siblings are available too, and honestly two kittens are almost always easier than one.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (North Metro Atlanta area — local adoptions only)
scoring_notes:
• Dog-tested, kid-friendly, litter-trained kitten with a Seinfeld name — maximum newsletter charm for a broad audience
• Highly adoptable profile with low friction; likely moves quickly so feature value is time-sensitive
• Recently arrived via animal control with siblings still available, suggesting minimal shelter wait

blurb:
This guy has been through more than most cats will ever see. Peeta came from Mostly Mutts originally as a kitten, got adopted, came back due to family changes, got adopted again, then ended up in emergency surgery after accidentally swallowing a string that wrapped around his tongue and made its way into his GI tract. That's a rough stretch for anyone. He's fully recovered now, and he's ready to actually stay somewhere for good.

He's about five and a half years old, around ten and a half pounds, and once he decides you're his person, he's all in. He was shy when he first got back to his foster home, which makes sense given everything he's been through. But he opened up fast. Now he follows his foster around looking for pets and winds himself around their feet when he wants attention. That's not a cat who's given up on people. That's a cat who keeps trying.

He's litter trained, got along with other cats in his previous home, and would likely do well with gentle kids too. He just wants consistent love and a place that sticks. If you've got a calm home and room for a loyal, affectionate companion, Mostly Mutts would love to set up a meet. His adoption fee is listed on the profile page.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (North Metro Atlanta area — local adoptions only)
scoring_notes:
• Twice-adopted, surgery-surviving cat with a resilience narrative that will emotionally hook readers
• Affectionate and socially compatible with cats and gentle kids, making him broadly placeable
• Cyclical return history signals a long, difficult road and creates genuine urgency for a permanent home
